title: Latency-budgeted quantization & batching roadmap
body:
Purpose
This memo captures a compact, operationalizable approach for translating a per-request latency budget (SLO) into concrete quantization, batching, and cache settings. Goal is to produce a table of recommended presets that product teams can apply to common archetypes (conversational low-latency, high-throughput embeddings, mixed interactive) and a short experiment plan + spreadsheet knobs to validate cost/latency tradeoffs.

High-level idea
1) Start from allowed p95 latency (L_target).
2) Budget out subsystems: network (L_net), model decode (L_decode), queueing/batch wait (L_batch), cache hit path (L_cache_delta).
3) For each hardware tier and model variant pick the largest quantization and batch target s.t. expected total latency <= L_target with margin.
4) Simulate cost using token throughput assumptions and expected cache hit rates; produce per-1M-token cost and latency percentiles.

Archetypes and suggested starting presets (apply tune via spreadsheet)
- Conversational, latency critical (p95 target 200ms):
  - HW: single H100 or A100 80GB (prefer H100 if available)
  - Model variant: base-llm / 16k context
  - Quantization: 8-bit per-channel with outlier clipping (q8_per_channel_clipped) as default; try q4_0 only if p95 < 140ms and cost pressure high
  - Batch target: 1-3 tokens per request (microbatching); batch_max 8
  - KV cache TTL: sticky session enabled, TTL 900s; encourage prefix caching on repeated prompts
  - Prefetch/warmup: static KV warmup on session start for expected warm prefixes (50–100 token prefetch)
  - Expected tradeoff: q8 yields ~1.5x cost reduction vs fp16 with negligible latency impact; q4 reduces cost further but increases decode variance

- Embedding / throughput oriented (throughput > 2000 reqs/s):
  - HW: multi-T4 / A10 setup; focus on dense throughput
  - Model variant: embedding-384/768 optimized
  - Quantization: aggressive 4-bit with channel folding (q4_1) accepted if accuracy loss within threshold for downstream retrieval
  - Batch target: large batches (64–512) depending on max sequence length; batch_max tuned for memory headroom
  - Cache: ephemeral result caching for duplicate inputs, TTL 3600s, expected cache hit rate assumed 5–15% unless input dedupe present
  - Expected tradeoff: aggressive q4 gives high cost wins, but bench for embedding drift on recall metrics

- Mixed interactive (conversational + occasional long generations):
  - Hybrid routing: low-latency route -> q8 small-batch; fallback route -> q4 high-batch for longer tails
  - Autoscaling policy: burst lanes with pre-warmed q4 workers for queued long-gen cases

Spreadsheet knobs and column schema (single sheet used for sweeps)
Columns to include (exact names expected by autotune scripts):
- scenario
- model_name
- hw_tier
- qconfig
- batch_target
- batch_max
- assumed_seq_len
- kv_cache_ttl_seconds
- cache_hit_rate_pct
- measured_p50_ms
- measured_p95_ms
- expected_cost_per_1M_tokens_usd
- notes

How to run a quick sweep (steps)
1) Pick scenario and model, choose 3 qconfigs (fp16, q8, q4) and 4 batch targets.
2) Use perf harness to replay a representative trace (ideally a 10k request set with sampled seq lengths).
3) Collect token-level latency traces, queuing times, GPU utilization, and KV cache hits.
4) Fill sheet and compute expected cost per 1M tokens using unit GPU-minute pricing.
5) Reject any combo where measured_p95_ms > L_target or GPU memory OOM observed.

Key heuristics we found useful (not exhaustive)
- For p95-sensitive flows, prefer smaller batches and safer quant (q8).
- For cost-first flows, do per-cohort q4 trials but gate by quality tests tied to eval prompt set.
- Use cache_hit_rate_pct in simulation with conservative lower bound (observed_rate - 10pp) to avoid optimistic cost estimates.
- Add an explicit warmup budget for cold starts: include a 5–10% latency uplift for cold VMs in the spreadsheet.

Experiment checklist (A/B plan)
- Canary traffic slice 1% with q8 small-batch vs baseline fp16: monitor latency p95, customer-facing errors, and retrieval QA for 2 days.
- 10% slice for q4 in embeddings with downstream recall test (NDCG@10 delta) before roll.
- Long-tail test: route requests predicted >512 tokens to q4 farm and measure end-to-end latency and cost per session.

Risks and mitigation
- Quality regressions from aggressive quantization -> always tie to eval suite and automated regression alerts
- Tail latency blowups when batch wait accumulates -> enforce batch_max and queue_depth SLOs; add early-eviction rules
- Cache poisoning / TTL mis-estimate -> conservative TTLs and audit logging of cache hits per route

Next steps / actionables
- Populate the spreadsheet template (I attached a minimal CSV in the product bucket: latency-budget-sweeper.csv) and run initial sweep for 3 models across A100/H100/T4 by 2025-03-07.
- Add two eval prompt sets for conversational quality regression checks (owner: Arjun).
- Implement the hybrid routing rules in staging and run 72h soak.

Notes to reviewers
- This is a practical, runnable starting point rather than a canonical best-of-all-worlds doc. Focus on the spreadsheet schema compatibility with our autotune tooling and clear pass/fail gating for p95.
- If you want I can convert the column schema to a JSON schema for the autotuner, but keeping as CSV makes spreadsheet reviews easier for product.

End.
